chapter_title: Concerning Four Hunters of Light and Four of Darkness.
chapter_note: This kephalaion is predominantly systematic cosmological-correspondential teaching: a fourfold “hunter / ship / sea / net” mapping for Light powers and a parallel fourfold mapping for Darkness powers. The main later layers are (a) a dialogue/frame apparatus (¶1, ¶7) and (b) beatitude-style exhortations (¶6, ¶12) plus a polemical/institutional application that identifies the Darkness-hunter with what “rules in every sect” (¶11). ¶4 largely preserves the same cosmic mapping style but includes an institutional identification (“holy church”) that appears to be a later application graft within an otherwise older correspondential unit.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (“Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples”) is compiling-community frame; it introduces the topic rather than expounding the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the First Man who was sent from the greatness. He threw himself down to the five storehouses of darkness, he caught and siezed the enmity [... ...] his net also [... ...] out over all the children of darkness [... ...]. His ship is his four sons who are swathed over his body. The sea is the land of darkness [... ...]; his net is [...] and his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural cosmology: named hypostasis (First Man), descent to the five storehouses, and tight correspondential identifications (ship/sea/net) wholly within the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The second hunter is the Third Ambassador. This one, for by his light image, which he revealed to the depths below, he hunted after the entire light that is in all things; as it is established in them. His net is his light image, [...] the whole universe and took it prisoner, to this likeness [... His] ship is his light ship. [The sea] is the universe [...] which were hunted after by his net [...] his [glorious] image.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmic mechanism (revelation of the Light Image; hunting the light “in all things”) with correspondential mapping (net/ship/sea) remaining cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is Jesus the Splendour, who came from the greatness, who hunts after the light and life; and he [...] it to the heights. His net is his wisdom, [the] light wisdom with which he hunts the souls, catching them in the net. The sea is the error of the universe, the law of sin [...], the souls that are drowning in it [...]. He catches them in his net. They are the souls [... th]em by his light wisdom.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the clause “His ship is his holy church [...]” as an institutional identification (cosmos→contemporary church) embedded inside an otherwise cosmic correspondential mapping (hunter/net/sea).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-like correspondential exposition (Jesus the Splendour as a cosmic redeemer hunting souls by Light-wisdom) is interrupted by an ecclesial insertion (“holy church”) that points outside the closed cosmic system, suggesting a later editorial application within the paragraph.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth hunter is the great counsel that [...] that lives in the circuit [...] ⟨p.29⟩ entire universe in it today. Yet, at the end, in the dissolution of the universe, this very counsel of life will gather itself in and sculpt its soul in the Last Statue. Its net is its Living Spirit, because with its Spirit it can hunt after the light and the life that is in all things; and build it upon its body. Its ship, in which it is established, is this light cloud whereby it itself travels in the five elements [...], the great fire that will burn all the buildings of [... ...] in its net is the light and the life. It can rescue and free it from all bonds and fetters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highly systematic eschatological cosmology (dissolution of the universe; Last Statue; Living Spirit; five elements; great fire) with internal correspondential identifications (net/ship) and process-description rather than exhortation/citation.
Beatitude/exhortation directed to the reader’s deeds and personal escape; shifts from cosmological description to moral address (second-person implied), typical of later pastoral application.
Second formulaic attribution (“Once again he speaks…”) plus transitional promise to teach the counterpart list; this is editorial scaffolding around the teaching blocks.

paragraphs.core_text: The first hunter is the King of they who belong to the darkness, who hunted after the living soul with his net at the beginning of the worlds. His net is his fire and his lust that he has put upon the living soul, with which he has entangled it [...], through all his powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-historical placement (“at the beginning of the worlds”) and internal mechanism (fire/lust as net) keep the mapping within the Darkness-side cosmology, not contemporary polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second hunter is the evil counsel that lives in [...] that hunts after the light [...] and [...] up from [...] the earths to heaven. It binds them with its powers, which bring them to the heavenly worlds above. Its net is [...] whereby they are drawn up from the abyss [to the heig]hts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmic mechanics (binding/drawing from abyss to heights; earths/heavens) presented as a structured “hunter/net” function; no audience address or institutional targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: The third hunter is lust [...] walks in every power of the flesh that walks [...] in the [...] the living souls [... ...] them in its bodies, which [... ...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Though fragmentary, the register remains within the cosmic-anthropological system (“powers of the flesh,” “living souls”) as a functional description of a Darkness-agent.

Editorial application/polemical identification: “rules in every sect,” “souls of people,” and the focus on “erroneous teaching” as contemporary institutional error shifts the mapping from cosmos→cosmos to cosmos→present religious landscape (diagnostic of later pastoral graft).
Closing beatitude aimed at the reader’s recognition/knowledge for salvation; hortatory conclusion rather than structural cosmological exposition.
